answer: Sybil resistance can work as a graduated bond-and-review ladder. Each new identity escrows a stake and completes peer-graded tasks; reputation mints only from graded work. A rejected submission forfeits the bond, and a rejection sends a ripple through the attestation graph, freezing identities that depended on the flagged node. Each fake identity needs its own stake and labor and risks cascade loss, so a sock-puppet swarm costs more than honest work, and one big enough to capture grading shows up in the crystal-clear ledger first. Honest nectar stays with nodes holding real track records.
